data.hypothesis: A factor-two target mapping with 256 threads (512 outputs per block) reuses each streamed source position and mass across two target accumulators while testing a larger CTA than the previously measured factor-two configurations. The larger CTA could affect scheduling or resource residency; prior factor-two candidates were valid but slower than baseline, so no speedup or occupancy effect is assumed. This path uses no shared-memory source staging.
data.notes: The previous valid factor-two configurations used 64 threads/128 outputs and 128 threads/256 outputs, both around 0.002617 seconds; the measured factor-four parent was around 0.004442 seconds, versus the baseline around 0.001847 seconds. This candidate isolates another factor-two launch shape. No register-count or occupancy measurement is available here; rely on controller build metadata if reported, and judge performance using the official timing metric after correctness checks.
transformations: Map two target particles per thread, with the second target index offset by blockDim.x; retain independent force accumulators and self-interaction checks.
Load each streamed source particle's position and mass once per loop iteration and reuse them across valid targets; keep shared-memory allocation at zero.
Set the launch to 256 threads and 512 logical outputs per block, and bounds-check both targets so arbitrary N and partial final blocks are covered.
